headline: High: Khoj’s broad network egress plus shared indexed notes create leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are lower because godot_rl_agents is read-only and non-networked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented shared channel or output parser surface, and B does not expose clipboard/MCP bridging by default. However, B reads indexed documents and can ingest file content as context, so if A’s outputs are manually copied into notes or docs, prompt injection becomes possible. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are copied into B-indexed notes or documents
IF B is configured to treat retrieved text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Disable indexing of untrusted A-generated text
Mark A outputs as data-only in the workflow
Use a separate notes collection for agent outputs
Add a manual review step before ingestion
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to retrieved chunks

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress, so it can transmit retrieved content to external services. A is open-source game-playing with no network egress, so it is not the leak source, but pairing it with B can expose any A-generated artifacts that are stored in B’s workspace. The shared-data pathway is plausible in default RAG use.
conditions: IF A-generated artifacts are stored in B-indexed notes or files
IF B is configured to use cloud search or external model providers
mitigations: Restrict B to self-hosted inference only
Exclude sensitive notes from indexing
Separate A artifacts into a non-synced workspace
Review outbound provider settings in B
requires-engineering: enforce per-collection egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write or git capabilities, while B explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is B’s read access to files, so the pair is mostly read-only from a coordination standpoint.
conditions: IF A is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants it write access not shown in the profile
IF B is paired with another writer against the same files
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same notes
Use read-only mounts for B where possible
Document that A has no write path
requires-engineering: add file-locking if write access is later introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s retrieval/chat workflow can treat indexed content as authoritative, and A can generate outputs that may be copied into those notes or docs. If B then summarizes or acts on that content without verification, errors can cascade into downstream work products. A is not action-taking, but B’s broad egress and retrieval make the propagation path realistic.
conditions: IF A outputs are ingested into B’s indexed documents
IF B is used to draft or act on retrieved content without human verification
mitigations: Require source-link verification before reuse
Keep A outputs in a separate review queue
Add a checklist for factual claims in B
Limit B to summarization, not action-taking
requires-engineering: add citation enforcement in the retrieval pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles personal notes, indexed documents, and model-provider API keys, while A is a game-playing repo with no data classes touched. The compliance risk is therefore concentrated in B: if personal or regulated notes are indexed and sent to external providers, residency/retention obligations can be breached. A is not the compliance driver here, so it is cited only to show the pair is otherwise low-risk.
conditions: IF regulated notes are indexed in B
IF B routes queries or embeddings to external providers without a DPA or residency controls
mitigations: Exclude regulated notes from indexing
Use self-hosted providers only
Rotate and protect API keys
Review retention settings in B
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
